name: Martu Wangka
catalog_quote: Stress usually on the first syllable. In words of more than 4 syllables there is often a secondary stress on the third. In words of 5 syllables the position of the secondary stress varies. (Marsh 1969:146) [...] Mantjiltjara may have ternary stress. The feet are syllabic trochees, assigned from left to right, with main stress falling on the initial foot. (Hayes 1995:365-366)

audit.reasoning: Identity: the catalog unit mart1256 'Martu Wangka' (this catalog record, source StressTyp2) is the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Mantjiltjara', i.e. the Manyjilyjarra dialect (Glottolog many1256, child of mart1256); the 2026-09-12 the full catalog pass already ruled roster key many1256 a duplicate entry of this unit (lang/many1256/), so no identity problem remains as long as many1256 is kept as an alias, not a second unit. Quote check: everything the record actually quotes is held by the project and verbatim — Goedemans 1998 App. D category I header (p.236) and the Mantjiltjara entry (printed p.238, record says p.239: fix the locator), Hayes 1995:100 list (33d) in the held ch.5 page pin, and the StressTyp2 entryin the StressTyp2 dump — but all of these are second-hand carriers of Marsh 1969:146, which nobody has read (JSTOR-only; the Rosetta excerpt I downloaded covers pp.131-139 and stops before the stress section). sources.quote: No stress rule in the excerpt; only incidental mentions ('[ɪ] tends to occur in stressed syllables', 'in certain instances when stress is shifted to the end of an intonation contour'). The p.146 statement banked by StressTyp2 remains unread.

sources.note: The sole dedicated phonology of the lect and the source every carrier (StressTyp2, Goedemans 1998, Hayes 1995) cites; our deciding text is StressTyp2's telegraphic paraphrase of p.146. Needed to pin the verbatim wording of 'usually', the 5-syllable exception (puˈɭikuˌruŋka, main stress on σ2) and the binary/ternary secondary pattern. Rosetta excerpt downloaded now stops at p.139.
